analysis: Examined .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml base and head. The only changes are line 59 (the `source` job) and line 519 (the `publish` job), both moving from the blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 runner to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04. The trust gate is unchanged: `source` still checks out master and runs verify-desktop-source before any signing credential is used. Secrets stay confined to the `sign` and `sign-dmg` jobs, which still run on the macOS blacksmith runners. `publish` keeps `contents: write` and still fetches artifacts by id and digest, then runs `sha256sum --check`. Neither moved job handles signing secrets. Switching to ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners does not widen the attack surface and slightly narrows third-party runner trust for the `contents: write` job. I found no regression against the retained provider threat model (A-017, T-054). The dev-branch workflow (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, unit 952343854b5413b6:0) was supplied only as metadata plus a truncated patch excerpt (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The visible part shows the trigger moving from a dev push to a 6-hourly schedule gate plus workflow_dispatch, with a gate job on master that dispatches on refs/heads/dev. That workflow calls the reusable release-provider.yml with signing secrets, so a later pass should check the new dispatcher job's permissions, its ref/SHA pinning, and whether dispatch or schedule can build a non-dev ref or an unreviewed commit. I could not verify any of that from the supplied evidence, so I record it as unverified rather than as a finding.
